annotations.text:
Two views, no toggle.
Your goal is two questions, so each gets a view that answers it — rather than one layout with a switch that makes the reader work out which mode to be in. Orientation is not a preference; it follows from the question.

RHYTHM — opens here. Time is the x-axis, which is the only way cadence is visible: 7–10 day releases through Feb–Mar, stretching to 24–36 days after the 2.0 fork. The cadence band above the graph makes that the headline rather than something you infer from tag dates.

CARRY-FORWARD — the audit. Vertical, one row per release, ancestry drawn as a connected spine. Two separate alarms now, where the old build conflated them into one scary number:
amber = shipped but develop has not seen it (23) — a forecast, 2.1 will regress them
red = in no branch and not in v2.0.1 (79) — actually gone

Explored and set aside. Branch lanes is the truest topology but needs a column per live branch, and opencrvs-core has 46. The status matrix reads fastest but shows no ancestry at all — it cannot tell you the 1.9 line forked away from 2.0, which is why the gaps exist. Kept for reference.
